claims.text: Transition-metal catalytic activity is governed by the dynamic interplay between metal oxidation state and surface adsorbate coverage.
Operando spectroscopy and microscopy can elucidate the interplay between oxidation state and adsorbate coverage.
The catalyst's active state is characterized by a specific metal oxidation state and surface adsorbate coverage.
Changing temperature, pressure, or reactant concentration perturbs the catalyst's active state and reaction mechanisms.
Operando spectroscopy and microscopy can probe catalyst active states and reaction mechanisms in real time.
Metal-adsorbate interactions involve the formation of surface intermediates.
Metal oxidation state influences adsorbate binding energies.
The interplay between oxidation state and adsorbate coverage influences the formation and stability of surface intermediates.
Changes in surface-intermediate formation and stability modulate catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability.
The perturbation will produce a 20% increase in catalytic activity relative to the baseline.
The perturbation will produce a 15% improvement in selectivity relative to the baseline.
Catalytic activity and selectivity can be assessed using reaction rates and product yields.
The baseline operates at approximately 250°C, 1 atm, and stoichiometric reactant concentrations.
The hypothesis is expected to hold from 200–300°C, 0.5–2 atm, and from stoichiometric reactant concentrations to a two-fold excess.
The nature of metal-adsorbate interactions and the effect of oxidation state on binding energy vary with the transition metal and reaction conditions.
Variation in metal identity and reaction conditions could alter the predicted activity and selectivity outcomes.
A perturbation of operating conditions can be designed to disrupt metal-adsorbate interactions.
Failure of perturbed activity and selectivity to deviate by more than 5% from baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
